races.name: Download The At The Races App Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Monsieur Kodi
runners_data.note: Mapped as prominent but will likely lead here given no genuine pace rival; 4/43 T14 strike rate for Fahey is modest but this horse has won twice on similar Standard AW going in recent history and has solid place form at 6f on this surface — the key runner for the dominant pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: A win three starts back followed a productive spell of places (3rd, 2nd) before it, though his last two efforts (7th, 4th) are more modest by comparison. Back after a 41-day break with prior form at today's trip and a figure of 79, he's a leading danger from stall 11 if he finds that earlier level again.

runners_data.name: Fifty Nifty
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with poor recent form (6-5-4-7-8) and zero wins from 3 runs on comparable Standard going; Martin Dunne's stable has only one runner in the 14-day window and this horse has not shown the tactical speed to deal with a moderately run 6f.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in his last five starts (8th, 7th, 4th, 5th, 6th), yet our figure of 82 - the second-highest in the field - suggests far more ability than that sequence shows. Fit again 28 days on with prior form at today's trip, he's arguably the leading danger from stall 3 if he can convert that promise.

runners_data.name: Hierarchy
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with 11 runs on Standard going and three wins in that context — the best course-going profile among the closers; William Carver takes the ride and the tongue-tie is retained, but finishing from rear requires a stronger pace than Monsieur Kodi is likely to set.
runners_data.comment: Top of our figures on 82, well clear of his 74 official mark, and he found the frame in each of his last two starts (4th, 3rd) either side of a flatter spell before that. Fit again 24 days on with prior form at today's trip, he's the one to beat from stall 4.

runners_data.name: Veydari
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who finished second at 6f on Good going last time, showing she can race close to the pace and quicken; Julie Camacho's yard is firing (1/17 T14) and at only one run on Standard going she represents a small unknown surface-wise, but her style suits this race shape well.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in his last five starts but he was runner-up last time out, a line that fits with a big figure of 81 - third-highest in the field. Back after 39 days with prior form at today's trip, he's up with the leading dangers from stall 13.

runners_data.name: Akabusi
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from Mike Murphy's yard with a strong record at 6f on Good, having won over this trip at three-year-old level; only 18 days since last run and tongue-tie worn, but his off-the-pace style is compromised by the lack of genuine early pace here.
runners_data.comment: A win four starts back is the standout in an otherwise modest sequence that includes three 8ths, and a figure of 77 rates him only fair for this field. Quick to back up after 18 days with prior form at today's trip, he looks workmanlike rather than a leading player from stall 7.

runners_data.name: King Of Chaos
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse whose last two wins came at 6f on Standard and Good respectively, showing genuine tactical versatility; 7 runs on Standard going with two wins and three places suggests he handles the surface, and Marco Ghiani is an astute judge of pace — capable of positioning closer if needed.
runners_data.comment: A win two starts back sits amid a run of modest finishes either side of it, and a figure of just 72 places him only mid-pack. Quick to reappear just eight days on with prior form at today's trip, he needs more than his recent efforts have shown to feature from stall 12.

runners_data.name: Twilight Madness
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse placed into midfield on the map; Charlie Tucker (7lb claimer) takes the ride for Simon Hodgson, who has had no runners in 14 days — 13 runs on Standard going with two wins and seven places is the strongest surface profile in the field, but 91 days off and the style mismatch in a slow-paced race are real concerns.
runners_data.comment: Well held in his last two starts (8th, 9th) and a figure of 69 puts him towards the foot of the field, though he was competitive enough with a win and three places before that. A 91-day break and that recent form make him hard to fancy from stall 5.

runners_data.name: Yachtsman
runners_data.note: Genuine closer whose natural position at the rear is compressed by the number of hold-up types in this field; Jonny Peate rides and the horse won over 6f on Good last time out, but only 2 from 9 on comparable going and the likelihood of sitting further forward than ideal muddies the tactical picture.
runners_data.comment: A win two starts back shows he retains some ability, though either side of it he's been no better than midfield (4th, 7th). Back after 57 days with prior form at today's trip and a moderate figure of 74, he's workmanlike rather than a leading player from stall 9.

runners_data.name: Veil Of Clouds
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old from Simon & Ed Crisford (6/21 T14, hot form) who has placed at 6f on Standard going and races prominently; 15 days since last run is fine, and the strong trainer angle combined with a pace-pressing style makes this one of the more interesting profiles in the field.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in her last three starts, she was runner-up two starts back, sandwiched between a pair of 5ths - a workmanlike level backed by a figure of 70. Quick to reappear after just 15 days with prior form at today's trip, she's respectable without standing out from stall 1.

runners_data.name: Obsidian Verse
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse who won at 6f on Standard going (1 from 6 on comparable surface) but is mapped to midfield here due to the overcrowded rear; James Fanshawe's yard is in form (4/15 T14) and Kaiya Fraser rides, but the style displacement reduces the chance of getting the run the horse needs.
runners_data.comment: A figure of 68 leaves him towards the bottom of this field, and a poor 8th three starts back is a concern, though he did win two starts back. Back after 34 days with prior form at today's trip, he needs to rediscover that level to feature from stall 10.

runners_data.name: Nebbia
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly who has placed at sprint trips on Standard going but has drifted up to 7f and back, and the redistribution to midfield means she won't get the closing run that suits her; Finley Marsh rides for Hughie Morrison, who has had no runners in 14 days, and the style-fit score of 0.90 is a meaningful flag.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in her last five starts, though she has been runner-up twice in that spell, including last time out. A figure of 67 puts her towards the foot of the field, and back after 39 days with prior form at today's trip, she's up against it from stall 2.

runners_data.name: Far Too Fizzy
runners_data.note: 112 days between runs is the longest layoff in the field and a significant fitness concern; David Loughnane has good recent numbers (4/14 T14) and this filly has won and placed at 6f on Standard, but the extended break combined with being a true closer in a likely-slow-pace race makes a bold showing difficult.
runners_data.comment: Bottom of our figures on 62 and a 112-day absence is a big ask fitness-wise, though a win four starts back shows there's some ability there. Modest recent form (5th, 3rd, 7th) either side of that leaves him hard to fancy from stall 6.

runners_data.name: Red Snapper
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old who won at 5f on Heathpark going but is a genuine hold-up type competing here at 6f on Standard AW for what appears to be the first time; Ben Ffrench Davis (5lb) rides for Kathy Turner (0/1 T14) and the combination of step up in trip and redistribution away from natural closing position are doubly problematic.
runners_data.comment: A moderate 7th last time out follows a much better sequence before it, including a runner-up spot two starts back and a win further back again. His figure of 75 rates him well above his 64 official mark, and fit again 28 days on with prior form at today's trip, he's not without claims from stall 8.

races.paceDynamic: Monsieur Kodi is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger disputing the lead, is set to control the pace from the front on what should be a relatively comfortable, measured gallop over this 6f Wolverhampton standard. Veydari and Veil Of Clouds are the likeliest runners to press or sit close to the tempo, giving Monsieur Kodi a small group around him but nothing that threatens to turn this into a scorching pace. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up horses — Yachtsman, Obsidian Verse, Nebbia, Twilight Madness, Far Too Fizzy, and Red Snapper are all genuine closers redistributed into midfield positions on the map because the race simply cannot accommodate that many at the rear; of these, Yachtsman and Obsidian Verse have the most tactical speed to push closer than their natural style, but most will be ridden further back than ideal. A controlled, sustainable pace set by a lone leader over 6f on an all-weather track typically compresses finishing positions and favours horses racing prominently or with a high cruising speed — closers who need a true end-to-end gallop to get into their best rhythm are disadvantaged here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kodi Controls, Proximity Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Monsieur Kodi sets an uncontested, measured pace and the race is decided by who can sustain momentum into the straight without needing a strong injection of pace.
scenarios.body: Monsieur Kodi travels comfortably on the lead and the horses closest to him through the race inherit the best position turning into the short Wolverhampton straight; proximity to the pace is the decisive factor.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Veydari or Veil Of Clouds travels smoothly in second or third and kicks off the steady pace to assert in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With Monsieur Kodi setting a manageable tempo, a prominently positioned horse with a good cruising speed can time an effort perfectly, needing no real finishing burst to overhaul the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves deceptively strong enough mid-race to string out the field, creating a clear late run for one of the closers who avoids traffic.
scenarios.body: Wolverhampton's tight turns can cause bunching, but if a gap appears in the final two furlongs, one of the true closers can land a telling late blow; Hierarchy has the best course-and-distance form profile among the hold-up contingent.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Monsieur Kodi is challenged unexpectedly early and the pace falters, causing a messy race in which nothing gets a clear run and a single rapid finisher picks up the pieces.
scenarios.body: A chaotic early fractions scenario is unlikely given the clear lead horse but could see an off-the-pace runner with a sharp sprint land a blow; King Of Chaos has the turn of foot to exploit a scrambled finish.

watchPoints.text: Veil Of Clouds (Crisford, 6/21 T14) races prominently on a pace-friendly track — the in-form trainer angle combined with a position close to Monsieur Kodi makes this a danger runner if the hot stable is pitching for a quick follow-up.

Twilight Madness has an exceptional 13-run Standard-going record (2W, 7P) but 91 days off, a 7lb claimer, and a true hold-up style in a likely slow-paced race mean that record may flatter the current situation — watch for whether the pace is strong enough for this horse to land a late blow.

King Of Chaos and Yachtsman are both genuine closers mapped closer to the pace than their natural position — if either jockey tries to compensate by pushing forward early, it could create mid-race congestion and interference in the final two furlongs.

Monsieur Kodi's T14 strike rate (4/43) is poor, but this horse is the entire fulcrum of the race shape — if it is slowly away or doesn't lead, the race structure breaks down completely and the scenario probabilities shift sharply toward hold-up horses.

Far Too Fizzy's 112-day absence is the field's longest layoff; David Loughnane's runners fresh can sometimes show well, but watch the market — if backed despite the break it signals stable confidence, which would upgrade the hold-up scenario probability.

races.name: Free Tips On attheraces.com Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Extended Credit
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and unraced officially at OR 120 — Rob Hornby and Charles Hills is a formidable combination for an unexposed type, and the unknown going tag is no concern on a synthetic surface that suits most; a natural unknown style means it could sit anywhere, but trainer's 3/22 14-day strike rate keeps interest high.

runners_data.name: One Of The Boys
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner, carrying a STYLE_FIT flag that suggests it may struggle if it cannot dominate from the front — two placed runs on this exact course and going (2/2 on sim-going) give it solid claims as pace-setter, and Finley Marsh should ensure it gets away cleanly to exploit the uncontested lead.

runners_data.name: Ridger
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with just one run, a sixth over 6f at Goodwood on Good — the step up to 7f on a synthetic surface is an unknown, and Ollie Sangster's yard has been firing with 4/19 in 14 days, but there is no Polytrack evidence yet to build confidence.

runners_data.name: Sonbelievable
runners_data.note: True hold-up runner whose best two runs came at 7f-8f on Standard and Soft; the sim-going record of 1/2 shows some ability to act on this surface, though ninth last time at Wolverhampton on Standard is a clear negative and Darragh Keenan will need luck in running.

runners_data.name: Cullinan Wolf
runners_data.note: Seb Spencer's four-year-old showed a tendency to fade in finishes on its only start, a distant eighth over 6f at Goodwood — though a natural hold-up horse in terms of style, the race shape pushes it forward into midfield where it must perform out of its comfort zone, and the STYLE_FIT discount applies.

runners_data.name: Rua Mor
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer whose record is largely built over much longer distances (16f heritage), and while two runs on Standard going show some versatility, dropping dramatically in trip to 7f on the Polytrack represents a significant unknown for Jonathan and Sam England.

runners_data.name: Carnival Of Light
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's four-year-old has back-to-back fourths over 8f at Goodwood on Good — the trip shortens here and, being a genuine hold-up type pushed into a midfield slot by the race's structure, the shorter trip and positional compromise both work against a horse that has shown only modest form so far.

runners_data.name: Time Alone
runners_data.note: Marco Ghiani takes the ride on an unraced debutant with a tongue-tie flag (hg:t) — Richard Newland & Jamie Insole operate at 2/22 over 14 days, which is modest, but lightly raced unknowns with top jockeys can spring surprises in maiden company and the tongue-tie suggests the yard has already schooled it carefully.

runners_data.name: Korbut
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's three-year-old is the form horse of the field by consistency — 0/2/5 placed from five runs with four sim-going efforts — yet its OR of only 72 against a field rated 120 all round is stark, and while naturally a hold-up type mapped into midfield here, Dylan Hogan will need the pace to collapse for Prescott's patient approach to pay off.

runners_data.name: Pink Pyjamas
runners_data.note: A complete debutant with no public form, Robert Havlin and Jack Morland (1/8 in 14 days) combining at maiden level; the unknown style and going tags mean it is impossible to place tactically, but debutants with experienced jockeys in small Polytrack maidens deserve a watching brief.

runners_data.name: Poets Praise
runners_data.note: Lightly raced Ralph Beckett three-year-old returning after a 266-day absence — the two previous runs both came on Soft at 7f with finishes of fourth and fifth, so the ability to handle a synthetic surface is unproven and the very long layoff is a significant risk factor despite Edward Greatrex being a capable pilot.

races.paceDynamic: One Of The Boys is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rivals looking to press from the front, should secure a clean lead and dictate a sustainable, uncontested gallop over seven furlongs on the Wolverhampton Polytrack. That controlled tempo — neither dawdling nor truly testing — typically compresses the field and leaves little room for hold-up horses to make up ground from the rear, meaning prominent or tracking runners who can sit just off the pace and travel into the contest are best placed. The field carries a significant cluster of hold-up types (Cullinan Wolf, Carnival Of Light, Korbut) who have been mapped to midfield because there is simply no room at the back of a true hold-up pack in a race with this much rear-end weight; all three are racing out of their natural role and should be discounted accordingly. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours horses that can race prominently or in mid-division and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — pure closers from the back will find the steady pace unhelpful.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Front Wins
scenarios.trigger: If One Of The Boys leads unopposed and the hold-up horses fail to close the gap set by a measured pace.
scenarios.body: One Of The Boys sets a sustainable gallop, the midfield pack tracks without threatening, and a horse racing prominently behind the leader produces the decisive turn of foot in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a lightly raced or unexposed runner travels smoothly just off the pace and picks off the leader inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: One Of The Boys does the donkey work but a well-bred debutant or lightly raced type with hidden ability locks on behind and surges late; the modest gallop sets up a finishing kick rather than pure stamina.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Suits Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow enough that genuine midfield horses can close powerfully from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Korbut, who has shown consistent placed form at this trip and going, or Rua Mor arrive with momentum on the outside and wear down the leader; redistribution means they are racing closer than usual, marginally aiding their chance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Folds, Hold-Up Lands
scenarios.trigger: If One Of The Boys hits the front too hard and weakens sharply, leaving a true hold-up horse to finish fastest of all.
scenarios.body: With Cullinan Wolf, Carnival Of Light and Korbut all forced into unnatural positions ahead of their comfort zone, the one who adapts best could snatch a place; however, the style mismatch makes this a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: One Of The Boys is the only confirmed front-runner — if it dwells or misses the break, there is no natural pace in this field and the race could turn tactical and messy, undermining every scenario built around a controlled lead.

Extended Credit, Time Alone and Pink Pyjamas are all debutants with unknown style tags — any one of them showing unexpected early speed could crowd One Of The Boys and artificially inflate the gallop, turning a steady race into a genuine test.

Korbut's significant OR gap (72 vs 120) versus the rest of the field needs watching — if Prescott has significantly improved this horse at home it could outrun its odds, but betting down a 48-point ratings gap purely on consistency is a material risk.

Cullinan Wolf, Carnival Of Light and Korbut are all racing out of their natural hold-up roles due to redistribution — watch whether they settle in their unnatural midfield positions early, as any fractious or reluctant behaviour could compromise their runs entirely.

The going is listed as unknown despite Wolverhampton being an all-weather Polytrack venue — confirm surface conditions before the off, as any unexpected cushion or kickback in the surface could particularly affect the hold-up horses making ground from behind.

races.name: attheraces.com/marketmovers Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Moostar
runners_data.note: Consistent recent form (322362) for James Owen with strong course fitness, but her true style is hold-up and the glut of closers in this field forces her into midfield rather than her preferred rear berth, which tempers confidence in her producing a finishing burst.|
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and rarely far away — five places from her last six starts — this filly is a picture of consistency even without a win in that spell. Quick to reappear just 11 days on with today's distance already proven, but turning those placings into a win is the query.

runners_data.name: Zarinca
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, Edward Bethell's filly won over 6f at this track on Standard and twice finished placed here — her T14 strike rate of 9/35 is respectable and she carries the key positional advantage of uncontested lead in a field that cannot disrupt her.|
runners_data.comment: Tops our figures for this field and joins a yard in red-hot form (26% winners in the last fortnight). She won three starts back and returns quickly, just 13 days later, with today's distance already proven — two moderate efforts since are the one blot.

runners_data.name: Fizzy Cristal
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's 3yo has two wins over 6f at this track on Standard, a 27-day break since last run, and races from a genuine hold-up position without the redistribution complication — she needs the pace to be honest enough to close but has the class to deliver.|
runners_data.comment: Second in our figures for this field with two wins in her last five starts, this filly has plenty of gears when in form and has raced over today's distance before. A modest fifth last time out is the concern, though a decent speed figure suggests she retains ability.

runners_data.name: Court Of Stars
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's filly has a strong 7f Standard record (one win, two seconds) and goes well on this surface; a prominent racer ideally suited to sit behind a lone front-runner and produce a clean sustained challenge through the final furlong.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth in our figures here, this filly won five starts back and followed up with back-to-back runner-up efforts, showing solid ability at her best. Her last two efforts (sixth, fourth) have been below that level, though she has raced over today's distance before.

runners_data.name: Eazy On The Eye
runners_data.note: Heather Main's 4yo carries 140lbs (top weight) and her trainer has a blank recent strike rate (0/4 in 14 days), but she showed resilience when third last time over 8f on Standard — the drop to 7f and a hold-up style mean she needs a truly run race to make her finishing effort count.|
runners_data.comment: Third in our figures for this field, rated well above her official mark despite patchy recent form — unplaced last time out with only one podium finish in her last five starts. Prior form over today's distance and that gap to the mark are the reasons to take a chance.

runners_data.name: Pickersgill
runners_data.note: Winner and twice placed over this exact 7f/STA configuration, Iain Jardine's mare has the course-and-distance profile to threaten, though her natural hold-up style gets squeezed into midfield by the volume of closers, meaning she'll need to produce from a position that isn't entirely her own.|
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and quick to run again just 12 days later, this filly has raced over today's distance before. Her only win in her last six starts came four starts back, sandwiched by a seventh and another runner-up effort, with a moderate speed figure of 64.

runners_data.name: So Sassy
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's 4yo returns after a 73-day break wearing a visor, and while her sim-going record is strong (11/15), the lengthy absence combined with being shuffled forward from her preferred rearward berth creates meaningful doubt about whether she can reproduce her best here.|
runners_data.comment: A runner-up effort five starts back is her best of late, with four finishes no better than fourth since and 73 days off the track now. She has prior form over today's distance and a fair speed figure, but is yet to win in that spell.

runners_data.name: Hamaleel
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's 3yo has an excellent record at 7f on Standard (multiple places including a win), races in blinkers, and occupies a genuine hold-up slot without redistribution pressure — her profile makes her one of the most credible threats to the prominent horses if any pace develops.|
runners_data.comment: Runner-up two starts back and generally consistent across her last six starts, this filly does have solid credentials, though last time out (sixth) was below that level. She has raced over today's distance before, but a yard currently blank from 21 runners this fortnight is a concern.

runners_data.name: Searchingtheblues
runners_data.note: Mark Usher's 4yo is the lowest-rated runner in the field (OR 61) and her trainer has no recent winners (0/7 in 14 days); she has been placed twice over 7f/STA but her redistribution from true hold-up to midfield compounds the challenge of landing a big blow from a wide-open mark.|
runners_data.comment: Ninth in our figures for this field, this filly has managed only two thirds among six starts lately, sandwiched by finishes as low as eighth and an unplaced effort. She has raced over today's distance before, but a modest speed figure of 64 sums up a tough task on the book.

runners_data.name: Show Me Gold
runners_data.note: Tom Dascombe's 3yo arrives in excellent recent form having won over 7f/STA last time out and placed four of her last five starts at this trip — a prominent racer with current form credentials who can slot in directly behind Zarinca and apply pressure at the business end.|
runners_data.comment: A winner last time out and no worse than fourth in her last four starts, this filly has solid form on paper. She is only tenth of eleven on our figures, though, rated a shade below her official mark, despite having raced over today's distance before.

runners_data.name: Molly Mac
runners_data.note: The least exposed runner on OR 54, Grace McEntee takes the ride for Micky Fenton whose strike rate is modest (0/4 in 14 days); placed four times in her last five including twice at 7f/STA, she is a natural hold-up filly who lands in midfield by necessity rather than design, which complicates how she finds her rhythm.|
runners_data.comment: Bottom of our figures for this field despite a tidy record — never worse than fourth in her last five starts — and quick to back up, just 10 days since her latest run. She remains winless in that spell, and a modest speed figure of 52 points to a clear ceiling.

races.paceDynamic: Zarinca is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner fillies' handicap over 7f at Wolverhampton, and with no other natural leader to pressure her, she is highly likely to dictate on a comfortable, sustainable gallop from the outset. Court Of Stars and Show Me Gold will press from prominent positions, likely sitting just behind Zarinca in the first two furlongs, giving the race a controlled but not frantic early tempo. From there, the pace map compresses significantly into midfield and hold-up territory, where Moostar, Pickersgill, So Sassy, Searchingtheblues and Molly Mac have been redistributed — these are genuine hold-up types who cannot all find their natural rear position in a field this size, meaning the tactical picture further back will be more muddled than it appears. A controlled, front-runner-friendly tempo strongly favours horses racing prominently who can exploit an uncontested lead, with the true hold-up horses facing an awkward reality of not finding the gaps that a fast-run race would normally create for them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Zarinca Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Zarinca is allowed to bowl along in front without serious challenge, setting a metronomic tempo that never truly tests her rivals.
scenarios.body: Zarinca's winning form at this track (1/6f/STA) and her current OR of 70 give her a strong base, and with no natural pace rival to push her into a red-hot gallop she can conserve energy and quicken when asked. Horses racing prominently just behind her — Court Of Stars and Show Me Gold — are ideally placed to pounce if she tires, making this a clean front-to-mid race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Zarinca sets a pace fractionally too strong for her own stamina over 7f, allowing Court Of Stars or Show Me Gold to reel her in through the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Court Of Stars has an excellent record in similar-going at this trip (1/7f/STA, two seconds at 7f/STA) and is well-placed tactically to time a run off the leader's back. Show Me Gold won her last start (1/7f/STA) and arrives in form, making her an immediate threat if she travels kindly in second or third.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is brisk enough to string the field out and create genuine gaps for a hold-up runner to exploit in the straight.
scenarios.body: Hamaleel is the most convincingly placed of the true hold-up types, with strong course-and-distance form (6/7f/STA, 2/7f/STA) and a headgear flag (b) that could sharpen her response — she has the profile to pick off tired rivals. Fizzy Cristal also owns course winning form (1/6f/STA twice) and, operating from a hold-up position with no redistribution flag, could find daylight if the pace proves genuine.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Mid-Pack Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed hold-up types clash for limited space, creating interference and a muddled mid-race dynamic that scrambles the outcome.
scenarios.body: With Moostar, Pickersgill, So Sassy, Searchingtheblues and Molly Mac all competing for positions they would not naturally occupy, traffic and interference become plausible, opening the race up to a surprising beneficiary. Eazy On The Eye, who showed ability when third last time (3/8f/STA) over a slightly longer trip, might be the horse most likely to slip through unnoticed if the mid-pack confusion creates an unexpected pocket.

watchPoints.text: Zarinca's ability to reach the front uncontested will define the shape of the entire race — watch whether Court Of Stars or Show Me Gold attempt to go with her early, as any sustained pressure in the first three furlongs could fundamentally change who wins.

With Moostar, Pickersgill, So Sassy, Searchingtheblues and Molly Mac all crowding into midfield rather than their natural hold-up positions, watch for traffic problems and interference between the 4f and 2f markers that could compromise multiple runners simultaneously.

So Sassy returns from 73 days off and is fitted with a visor — watch her behaviour in the preliminaries and the first two furlongs, as a rusty reappearance in an unfamiliar positional role could see her drop out early.

Court Of Stars and Show Me Gold both have winning form over 7f on this surface and are natural prominent racers — watch whether either drifts left or right rounding the bend if the pace compresses the field, as Wolverhampton's track configuration can cause interference in a bunched midfield.

Eazy On The Eye carries 140lbs as top weight, the heaviest in the field — watch whether that burden visibly affects her action after the 3f marker, as it has contributed to her fading late in past runs over this distance.

races.name: Free Race Replays On attheraces.com Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Go Rimbaud
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's three-year-old brings a course-and-distance win (1/8f/STA) into this race and a solid 3/5 similar-going record; prominent racing style suits a tracking role directly behind Brocklesby Bill, and 83 days off is worth monitoring but the yard's 7/16 T14 strike rate suggests the horse is ready.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back, after a pair of runner-up efforts in the two starts before that, though he rounded off with a below-par 5th last time out after an 83-day layoff. Clear on our figures at 89 - well above his 82 official mark - he's the one to beat in this Class 4 event, with prior form at today's trip in his favour.

runners_data.name: Brocklesby Bill
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will set the pace, though flagged as racing out of its optimal style role at this trip — the 10f defeat at Goodwood raises stamina questions over a mile-and-a-half, and Kathy Turner has only one runner in the T14 window; Ben Ffrench Davis's 5lb claim is a useful weight relief.
runners_data.comment: He was runner-up last time out, and a winner two starts back, though an unplaced effort further back tempers that form, and his figure of 70 sits well below his 83 official mark, leaving him fourth of four on our figures. Fit again 25 days on with prior form at today's trip, he's the type to note if he can bridge that gap.

runners_data.name: On The Inlet
runners_data.note: Dr Newland & Insole's gelding is genuinely a prominent-style runner whose preferred racing position is denied here by the competition for the front rank — forced to settle in midfield, its two wins from a similar standard and a 2/22 T14 figure are solid credentials undermined by an unfavourable race shape.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins three and four starts back show he's capable at this level, even though his last two efforts (5th, unplaced) have been below that. A figure of 85, well clear of his 81 official mark, backs the better form, and fit again 51 days on with prior trip form, he's a leading danger if he rediscovers that level.

runners_data.name: Chapter
runners_data.note: The only true hold-up runner in this four-horse field, Chapter has two wins and a placed effort in its last five, but its single similar-going run returned nothing; wearing blinkers and ridden by Rob Hornby, it needs the pace to truly collapse to get competitive from off the bridle in a small field.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, backing up a similar success four starts back either side of a mixed middle spell (6th, 3rd), and a figure of 86 - well clear of his 79 official mark - marks him out as a leading danger. Fit again 35 days on with prior form at today's trip, he arrives with the profile of a horse on the upgrade.

races.paceDynamic: Brocklesby Bill is the confirmed front-runner and will set a sustainable, uncontested pace over this mile-and-a-half trip at Wolverhampton, with no genuine rival likely to challenge for the lead from the start. Go Rimbaud will track closely in a prominent position, while On The Inlet — a natural prominent type — is displaced to midfield due to the field holding more pace-seeking horses than the race shape can accommodate, leaving Chapter as the lone genuine hold-up runner from the back. This field holds more prominent types than can all secure their natural positions, with Brocklesby Bill and Go Rimbaud most likely to actually claim the front two slots, leaving On The Inlet squeezed back against its preferred role. A steady-to-moderate gallop set by a single front-runner over a stamina-testing distance favours a horse that can track the leader closely and sustain its effort through the final two furlongs — the prominent-to-tracking profile is the clear beneficiary here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled lead, tracker wins
scenarios.trigger: If Brocklesby Bill leads at a steady clip and Go Rimbaud tracks throughout, the race becomes a sustained stamina test from two out.
scenarios.body: Brocklesby Bill dictates a manageable fractions, and Go Rimbaud — fresh from a win at this venue and trip — has the prime position to pounce entering the straight; horses unable to get their natural prominent slot are at a disadvantage in a pace-controlled contest.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-runner lasts home
scenarios.trigger: If Brocklesby Bill bowls along at a true gallop and none of the others press, the leader conserves enough to sustain the effort all the way to the line.
scenarios.body: A solo front-runner on an all-weather track at a measured pace can use the rail to its advantage; Brocklesby Bill's recent Goodwood win shows it can see out a trip when conditions suit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer swoops late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race and the prominent horses hit the front too early, the hold-up runner is gifted an opportunity from the back.
scenarios.body: Chapter owns two wins and a third from its last five and has previously delivered a late run; however, a small field with a single genuine hold-up runner means there is little cover and the pace must genuinely collapse for this to materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent scrap, pace collapse
scenarios.trigger: If On The Inlet fights for position against its natural instincts and causes a fractious early contest, the rhythm breaks and an unexpected order emerges.
scenarios.body: This depends on On The Inlet racing outside its mapped role in a chaotic fashion, a scenario that requires a low-probability combination of rider decision and race circumstance; Chapter would be the primary beneficiary of any collapse in tempo.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether On The Inlet attempts to reclaim its natural prominent position early — if Marco Ghiani pushes forward, a brief duel with Brocklesby Bill could disrupt the anticipated steady gallop and alter the entire race shape.

Brocklesby Bill's stamina over a mile-and-a-half is unproven — its form high over 10f at Goodwood ended in a 10th-place finish, and if it weakens sharply from two furlongs out, Go Rimbaud and Chapter are best placed to capitalise.

Go Rimbaud returns after 83 days off; watch the market closely at declaration — if the Gosden yard has trained it forward the price will shorten, but an undercooked favourite risk exists over this stamina trip.

Chapter's blinkers are worth noting as a first-time-headgear angle in a small field — if they sharpen its early response, the horse could engage more prominently than its hold-up label suggests, muddying the tactical picture.

runners_data.name: Scottish Anthem
runners_data.note: Stuart Edmunds' 7-year-old is a hold-up performer who has shown zero wins or placings on comparable good-to-firm/firm going in five attempts (0W0P sim-going), and 45 days off plus top-weight conditions make improvement hard to project; needs a truly run race this field may not provide.
runners_data.comment: His last two starts (7th, 9th) read poorly, though a 4th and 3rd further back and a big figure of 89 - well above his 83 official mark - suggest he's better than that recent slide indicates. Fit again 45 days on with prior form at the longer trip, he's second on our figures despite the modest recent form.

runners_data.name: Cabrera
runners_data.note: Rob Hornby takes the ride for Edward Bethell's yard, which is in fair recent form (9/35 T14), and this horse has placed twice at 1m2f on standard AW going — however all his recent runs have been at shorter than this 1m6f trip, and the step up in distance is a major unknown.
runners_data.comment: Top of our figures on 90, just a pound ahead of the next best and well above her 82 official mark, with her trainer also in good form on a strong recent strike rate. She is without a win in this sequence and a below-par last start (9th) is a mild concern, but with prior trip form, she's narrowly the best of these on figures.

runners_data.name: St Mawes
runners_data.note: George Scott's 4-year-old has a strong distance profile — winning twice over 1m6f on good and standard going — and his two placed efforts at 1m6f on similar surfaces (1W1P sim-going) underline that this trip on this type of surface is squarely in his wheelhouse; Darragh Keenan's book of rides suggests quiet confidence.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins three and four starts back underline solid form at this trip, and he's followed up with a 3rd and 2nd since, with a figure of 84 sitting above his 81 official mark. Fit again 56 days on, he's respectable without being amongst the most fancied, ranking only sixth in this deep field.

runners_data.name: Mersea Island
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's yard is in excellent form (7/66 T14) and this horse boasts a standout AW record at 1m2f-1m4f with two wins on standard (2W4P sim-going), but 212 days off is a significant fitness flag and the step to 1m6f asks a fresh question at top weight; the form figures over shorter suggest class is there if fit.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in this sequence (two and four starts back), either side of a runner-up effort show solid form, even though his last start (4th) was a slight dip. A figure of 86 matches his official mark exactly, but a 212-day absence is the concern - with prior form at the longer trip, he's a leading danger if fully wound up.

runners_data.name: Heathen
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's 7-year-old is the race's confirmed front-runner and has strong course-surface form (11/15 sim-going, 2W4P), giving him every chance to exploit an uncontested lead; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) reflects a listed positional note rather than a meaningful concern here since he is genuinely taking the lead role.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in this sequence but rarely far away, with a runner-up effort four starts back and finishes of 3rd or 4th either side, backed by a big figure of 88 above his 86 official mark. Fit again 48 days on with prior form at today's longer trip, that consistency makes him a leading danger on figures alone.

runners_data.name: Arcturus Flame
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes' 4-year-old has headgear (p) fitted and has been placed twice from four starts on good ground this summer, but is a genuine prominent racer who is unlikely to get anywhere near the front in this pace-heavy field — his chance is structurally undermined unless the map reshapes itself in running; 16 days since last run is a positive freshness angle.
runners_data.comment: Rarely too far away despite being without a win, with a runner-up effort two starts back among a string of 3rd and 5th finishes. A figure of 83, well above his 75 official mark, hints at more to come, and quick to reappear after 16 days with prior trip form, he's of some interest without being fully convincing.

runners_data.name: Gentle Warrior
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke sends out this 4-year-old who went from a career-best second over 1m4f at Goodwood back to a disappointing sixth — headgear (p) noted — and while naturally a horse who wants to race close to the pace, finding that position in this field is far from guaranteed; 5lb claimer Jack Nicholls takes off some weight which helps on paper.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in this sequence, his last start (6th) following a modest 4th, though a runner-up effort three starts back and a figure of 85 - a big leap above his 73 official mark - suggest real untapped potential. Fit again 32 days on with prior form at today's longer trip, he's an interesting midfield type on figures alone.

runners_data.name: Dance Time
runners_data.note: David Loughnane's 6-year-old has a deceptively good AW record (3W5P sim-going) but most of that form was delivered when she was able to race prominently and dictate; pushed back from her natural position by a crowded pace map, her chance hinges on getting closer to the front than the current race shape permits, and recent form figures (3-7-9-5-4) show inconsistency.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in this sequence, a modest 3rd last time out follows two well-beaten efforts (7th, 9th) before that, and a figure of 78 - though above her 72 official mark - still ranks last in this field. Fit again 32 days on with prior form at today's longer trip, she's hard to fancy on this form.

races.paceDynamic: Heathen is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival likely to challenge for the lead from the outset, should be able to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m6f trip. St Mawes and Cabrera are the most credible prominent types capable of securing early positions just off Heathen's shoulder, but Arcturus Flame, Gentle Warrior, and Dance Time are all natural prominent racers who cannot all occupy that ground — at least one or two will be forced to race further back than they prefer, effectively crowding the midfield. This creates a race that is likely to be run at a steady-to-fair clip rather than a genuinely searching pace, with Heathen dictating terms and the race potentially being decided by who can quicken from a compact group entering the straight. That profile favours horses with tactical versatility who can travel prominently or at least close to the pace — genuine hold-up horses who need a strong gallop to reel back the leaders are at a structural disadvantage in this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Heathen Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Heathen leads comfortably at a measured gallop and the race is not truly contested until the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Heathen dictates from the front without pressure, setting a pace that suits his stamina profile, and the race becomes a tactical test in the straight where positional advantage counts for everything. Horses who travel prominently and can quicken from close range — St Mawes and Cabrera — are best placed to mount a challenge, while true hold-up types lack the fuel injection they need.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Bunch Kick Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the race bunches up early and multiple horses share the lead, turning the race into a sprint from 3f out.
scenarios.body: The crowding of prominent types forces a compressed midfield and when the tempo lifts in the straight, the group races together rather than one horse dominating — favoring those with the best turn of foot at this trip. St Mawes, who has won twice at this distance, and Mersea Island, whose AW form is strong, emerge as the most likely beneficiaries of this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If an unusually strong early pace develops and the front-runners burn each other out, leaving a genuine gap for closers.
scenarios.body: Should the prominent types push harder for position than expected and compromise Heathen's ability to control tempo, the pace could become genuinely taxing over 1m6f. Scottish Anthem and Mersea Island are the truest hold-up profiles in this field, though Mersea Island's long absence (212 days) introduces a fitness question that tempers confidence here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed prominent types — Arcturus Flame, Gentle Warrior, or Dance Time — manages to secure a better early position than the pace map suggests.
scenarios.body: Should the race develop in a way that allows one of these natural front-runners to slot in closer to the pace than anticipated, their natural racing style would be working with them rather than against them. Arcturus Flame, who placed twice on good ground this summer, and Gentle Warrior, who struck a career-best when second over 1m4f, would be the most dangerous of the three in this low-probability shape.

watchPoints.text: Heathen — watch whether he is allowed to stride away unchallenged in the opening half-mile; if any of the redistributed prominent types push forward aggressively to dispute the lead, the scenario changes significantly.

Mersea Island — 212 days off for Charlie Johnston's yard warrants a close inspection in the paddock; if he shows any signs of ring-rustiness early, his hold-up profile leaves him with no margin for error.

St Mawes — having been off 56 days, watch for whether Darragh Keenan positions him immediately behind Heathen in the first half-mile; failing to secure that prime tracking spot would compromise his chance in a steady-pace scenario.

Arcturus Flame, Gentle Warrior, Dance Time — monitor the first two furlongs closely to see how aggressively these three compete for prominent positions; if more than one pushes forward hard, the early pace lifts and the scenario shifts toward Scenario C.

runners_data.name: Applesandpears
runners_data.note: Wins on this surface at 7f (STA) and has back-to-back wins in similar conditions — Rob Hornby keeps a prominent position naturally and this horse is one of the two most likely to actually hold a genuine early berth behind Special Dividend.|
runners_data.comment: Sitting second in our figures for this field, this filly has landed twice in her last five starts and joins a yard in red-hot form (26% winners in the last fortnight). A below-par sixth last time out is the concern, though she has raced over today's distance before.

runners_data.name: Augustus Gloop
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3yo with solid AW form at 6f — stepping up to 7f here and 135 days off is a concern, though Fanshawe's yard is operating at 4/15 over the fortnight; the natural prominent style suits the race shape but the absence and trip extension are risk factors.|
runners_data.comment: Won four starts back, and runner-up either side of it, but this gelding's last two runs (seventh, sixth) dipped below that level, and he is 135 days off that latest outing. Prior form over today's distance is there, but a mid-pack figure reflects the recent dip.

runners_data.name: Hungarian
runners_data.note: Consistent placer that genuinely wants to race prominently — in this field, forced into a midfield slot against its natural instincts, which blunts its effectiveness; Lemos De Souza's small yard at 2/5 T14 is a small positive but limited course form at 7f STA makes it hard to get excited.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out and never worse than fifth in his last five starts, this gelding is rated well above his official mark on our figures. Winless across that spell is the concern, along with a 46-day break since his latest run.

runners_data.name: Do Bronxs
runners_data.note: A hold-up type wearing a hood, trained by Loughnane who fires these horses fit quickly (4/14 T14) — needs the pace to be strong enough to reel in tiring leaders but the anticipated sustainable gallop is the wrong shape for this runner.|
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out, but runner-up two starts back, this gelding tops our figures for this field. Winless in his last five starts, yet he has raced over today's distance before and is fresh only 20 days off his latest run — the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Special Dividend
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter — won twice on this surface at 6f STA and has the front-running profile to dictate, though the step to 7f is untested in winning form and a STYLE_FIT tag suggests its chance could be compromised if the race shape turns against it; tongue tie applied.|

runners_data.name: Bone Marra
runners_data.note: Three wins and four places on AW surfaces, including a 7f STA win, gives this horse strong course-and-distance credentials — Sangster at 4/19 T14 is respectable and the tongue tie is a constant; one of two most likely to actually hold prominent ground in this race.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and successful twice in his last five starts, this gelding brings solid form into this and has raced over today's distance before. Only a midfield figure on our book, though, and 29 days have passed since that latest win.

runners_data.name: Deluded
runners_data.note: Good recent form with a win on AW (7f STA) and multiple placed efforts — a genuine front-runner by nature but shuffled into midfield by the depth of prominent horses in this field, which means racing out of role and at a discount to its true probability.|
runners_data.comment: Only seventh of nine on our figures, this gelding is hard to fancy on the book here. He does have a pair of thirds in his last two starts and prior form over today's distance, but his sole win in that spell came five starts back.

runners_data.name: Trust Amy
runners_data.note: Consistent at 6f but has never won, and all five recent runs show zero wins or places on AW (0W0P sim-going) — the step to 7f and a hold-up style in a race with a controlled pace are both negatives; Hanmer's modest T14 strike rate of 1/7 offers little confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, a clear step up on her previous four runs, this filly is rated well above her official mark on our figures with a strong speed figure to back it up. She is winless across that spell, but the leap forward last time stands out.

runners_data.name: Boy Named Sioux
runners_data.note: Has a win on AW at 7f STA in recent history which is the key positive, but 106 days off and a hold-up style make this a difficult proposition in a race that may not generate the pace needed; Fahey's yard at 4/43 T14 is a modest return.|
runners_data.comment: Second from bottom of our figures here, this gelding carries a modest speed figure of 64 and is 106 days off his latest run. He did win three starts back and has raced over today's distance before, but there is work to do to feature.

runners_data.name: Espona Bay
runners_data.note: Strong AW record with 1W5P in 11 similar-going runs — a natural prominent racer whose instincts are suppressed by the crowded front end, but of the three redistributed types this horse has the most compelling course-going form to recover if any gaps emerge; Dixon at 3/17 T14 is workmanlike.|
runners_data.comment: Bottom of our figures for this field despite a consistent record — no worse than fourth in each of his last five starts, including a win two starts back. He does have prior form over today's distance, but a modest speed figure of 64 leaves plenty to find here.

races.paceDynamic: Special Dividend is the confirmed pace-setter and will break from the gates to establish the lead, with Applesandpears and Bone Marra likely to slot in directly behind in the early prominent positions. The pace will be sustainable rather than scorching — Special Dividend has led before without being pressured, and with no genuine challenger willing to take them on, the gallop should be steady-to-honest over seven furlongs on this flat Wolverhampton surface. This field holds more prominent types than can realistically secure a forward position: Hungarian, Deluded, and Espona Bay are all natural front-runners or prominent racers who will be shuffled back into midfield against their instincts, with Applesandpears and Bone Marra best placed to actually hold the positions closest to the leader. The resulting shape — a controlled tempo with a genuine pace-setter dominating the early fractions — strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or just off the pace and finish with something in reserve, rather than hold-up types who need a strong gallop to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dividend Controls, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Special Dividend dictates a comfortable fractions and the race is won by a horse travelling just off the pace without expending energy chasing.
scenarios.body: Special Dividend sets an uncontested lead from the gate, with Applesandpears and Bone Marra the two most likely to hold genuine prominent berths and arrive with enough gas to challenge in the final furlong; the steady gallop means hold-up horses are never truly invited into the race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Sneak
scenarios.trigger: If Special Dividend sets a truly crawling pace that causes a bunched finish and allows the hold-up horses to produce late momentum.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow tempo creates a sprint finish from two furlongs out, giving Do Bronxs and Boy Named Sioux their best chance to close from off the pace with a clean run through; however, this shape depends on the front-runner setting a genuinely inadequate pace, which is against the evidence of a sustainable lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Recover Ground
scenarios.trigger: If Hungarian, Deluded, or Espona Bay manage to slot closer than expected and race more prominently than their mapped position suggests.
scenarios.body: Should the field string out early and gaps appear, one of the redistributed prominent types could recover to a position where their natural forward style is rewarded; Espona Bay's strong course and distance form on this surface makes it the most plausible beneficiary among the three if the race runs to suit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Front-Runners Weakened
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop proves stronger than anticipated and Special Dividend pays for a fast pace, allowing a hold-up finisher to reel in tiring leaders.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected tempo could expose a tiring Special Dividend inside the final two furlongs, with Do Bronxs or Boy Named Sioux best positioned to capitalise on a flat-out finish; this scenario is the least likely given the confirmed sustainable nature of the pace and the absence of any horse likely to press Special Dividend hard.

watchPoints.text: Special Dividend's ability to get 7f on AW is unproven in winning form — if it ties up inside the final furlong after dictating, Applesandpears and Bone Marra are the immediate threats to capitalise.
Hungarian, Deluded, and Espona Bay are all natural prominent racers forced into midfield — watch for scrimmaging or bumping as any of them attempts to recover position in the early stages.

Augustus Gloop returns after 135 days off and steps up in trip — if Fanshawe has had it tuned up, it could outrun a bigger price, but the combination of absence and trip extension makes it one to monitor rather than trust.

Do Bronxs is fitted with a hood for the first time and trained by a yard that has runners firing fit (4/14 T14) — the headgear change could sharpen a hold-up horse that needs to be alert from the start, particularly if the pace is less steady than expected.

Boy Named Sioux returns after 106 days off — if the Fahey yard has freshened this horse with a long break, a win at this track and trip in its recent history means it should not be entirely ignored if it shows signs of life in the market.
